consensus_summary: Iron primarily symbolizes strength, hardness, and unyielding/crushing power, especially severe rule or judgment (rod of iron; Daniel’s iron kingdom), with common secondary senses of oppression/affliction and mutual sharpening.
book_summary: Iron denotes the crushing strength of Daniel’s fourth kingdom, identified as Rome, the empire in power at Christ’s coming.
consensus_core_identification: strength/hardness/unyielding crushing power (of rule, kingdoms, or judgment)
book_core_identification: crushing strength of Daniel’s fourth kingdom (Rome)
boundary_disagreement: Consensus applies the strength/hardness register broadly (messianic rod of iron, oppressive yokes, stubbornness, etc.); the book restricts the term to the single historical case of Daniel’s fourth kingdom as Rome.
rationale: Both share the Daniel 2 crushing-strength image as central. The book keeps that referent but narrows the glossary sense exclusively to the fourth kingdom/Rome, excluding the wider primary applications (rod of iron, general severity) and alternatives that the consensus treats as standard. This is boundary refinement, not replacement of the core.
strongest_objection: The printed references omit the dominant rod-of-iron texts and include Dan 8:20-21 (Medo-Persia/Greece), which do not themselves establish iron or the Roman identification.
